title: Transit operations quality-control fragments - historical evidence
summary: Restricted corrective-action cases plus historical job descriptions expose reusable controls around deposits, trip/referral processing and schedule ownership. The evidence is strong enough to model the historical workflow, but exact current procedures and system rules remain unresolved.

claims.claim: Historical case evidence treats timely/daily deposit handling as an operational requirement; a formal corrective plan in 2015 required future deposits to be made daily, and a separate 2013 case identified untimely deposit handling as a concern.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2013/2015 cash-deposit cases - generalized control only

claims.claim: Historical RTEC administrative/accounting job-description material independently includes recording and verifying daily deposits, matching deposit slips to system data and responsibility for accurate cash-fare/receivable handling.

evidence.page_or_section: miscellaneous historical administrative/accounting descriptions - daily deposits/cash fares
evidence.note: Historical job descriptions; current role ownership must be validated.

claims.claim: A 2014 corrective record shows a transportation referral was expected to be followed up and released rather than left pending; it also states that a stamped signature on that referral was not acceptable under the then process.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2014 referral-processing counseling record - generalized workflow
evidence.note: Current signature/authorization requirements are not established by this historical case.

claims.claim: Historical CSR job descriptions independently show CSR duties including Medicaid/Waiver eligibility checks, passenger-profile updates, scanning physicians' statements/referrals/urgent-care statements and making/canceling transportation appointments, corroborating referrals as part of the CSR operational workflow.

A 2013 management counseling record treats a high number of still-unscheduled trips late in the scheduling process as a performance concern and states that the manager was expected to work/manage the schedule rather than depend on others to complete it.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2013 scheduling counseling record - generalized expectation
evidence.note: The record also notes the employee was new to the role, which is relevant context rather than a general exception.

claims.claim: A separate 2013 verbal-warning record shows that canceling a trip and rebooking it to the same bus the next morning created downstream scheduling problems and required another driver to be reassigned.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2013 trip-rebooking warning - generalized operational effect

claims.claim: Historical management job-description material includes monitoring trip timeliness, schedule gaps, idle time, breaks, no-shows, cancellations and unaccommodated trips, corroborating schedule quality/control as a management responsibility.

evidence.note: Current role owner/version must be validated.

claims.claim: A 2012 dispatch/case record treats correct completion of trip records and accurate no-show attribution as an operational quality control: an incomplete trip record could make the system appear to show an RTEC error when the client had not appeared.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2012 dispatch-error counseling record - generalized record-integrity issue

trigger: Cash/deposit handling, transportation referral processing or trip scheduling requires operational completion/quality control.
prerequisites: Use current system/procedure and current role ownership.
Maintain restricted handling of client/medical/referral information.
steps: Capture/refine the trip/referral/deposit transaction in the authoritative system.
Complete required validation/follow-up rather than leaving the item pending.
Reconcile deposits/cash records to the controlling system and supporting slip/record.
Escalate anomalies before they create missed trips, cash exposure or client-service failure.
decisions: Whether a referral/authorization is complete and acceptable.
Whether schedule changes create downstream coverage conflicts.
deadlines: Historical evidence implies daily/timely deposits and timely referral/schedule follow-up; exact current cutoffs require present-day procedures.
controls: Do not treat historical signature rules or individual corrective plans as current unless corroborated.
Preserve training/new-role context when evaluating errors; a single error does not by itself establish a universal discipline rule.
Use current role/system authority before automating financial or client-service decisions.
Trip/no-show records should reflect the actual service outcome accurately so reporting does not misattribute operational failure.
unresolved_questions: What current procedure defines referral acceptance/release and acceptable signatures/authorizations?
Which current roles own daily deposit collection, verification and reconciliation, and what are the cutoffs?
What current scheduling system/control flags unassigned trips, gaps, cancellations and rebook conflicts?
What current escalation path applies when a high-priority trip/referral is discovered unresolved?
automation_candidates: Referral aging/exception queue that flags unreleased referrals and missing/invalid authorization before service date.
Schedule-quality monitor for unassigned trips, rebooking conflicts, gaps/no-shows/cancellations and high-priority trips.
Daily deposit reconciliation workflow matching source cash/fare records to deposit slips and system totals with exception routing.
Role-aware operational checklist that uses training/tenure context for coaching but never auto-selects discipline.
Validate trip completion/no-show status before closure and flag records whose status conflicts with dispatch/client outcome evidence.

provenance.notes: Employee/client identities and case details excluded.
Job descriptions are historical/version-aware and do not establish present owner by themselves.
